solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gentry appear almost vulgar taking against Conservative leader

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short of its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: to appear is to arise, as a problem might
against can mean to, as in holding your ear to (against) the wall

indicators.note: the leader of Conservative is its opening letter

parts.note: racy means risqué or vulgar

explanation.surface: Toffs look slightly common when they side against the head of the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ARISE to ARIS; 'taking' is a link word, with RACY (vulgar) taking TO and C ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the gentry and the aristocracy are both the titled, landed upper class.

clue.text: Bank's ruse preceding ruin brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top
preceding puts the ruse piece before the ruin piece

parts.note: a trap is a ruse to catch someone
to mar is to spoil or ruin

explanation.surface: A bank's dodge, followed by its collapse, is raised in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests finance; it is an earth bank. 'brought up' reverses TRAP + MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall of raised earth, a fortified bank or embankment.

clue.text: One hangs revolutionary South American up outside prison

indicators.note: outside means the reversed letters go around the word for prison
up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary leftist
a pen is slang for a prison, short for penitentiary

explanation.surface: A Latin American rebel is jailed and someone ends up on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One hangs' is not a hanged man but a stocking suspender. 'up' reverses the whole run of revolutionary, South and American, and 'outside' wraps it round the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a strap that dangles from a belt to hold up stockings, so it is something that hangs.

clue.text: Last of hops put in grain kilns

indicators.note: put in means the chosen letter is placed inside the word for grain

parts.note: oats are a cereal grain

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of hops is used

explanation.surface: A farmer puts the end of the hop crop in with the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasts are kilns for drying hops, familiar in Kent as oast houses with cowled roofs.

clue.text: Fabulous bird snares chap with eye-opening charm

indicators.note: snares means catches inside, so the bird's name surrounds the word for chap

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights
a man is a chap
the opening of the word eye is its first letter

explanation.surface: A legendary bird traps a fellow with dazzling allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opening' looks like astonishing; it gives E, the first letter of eye.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to romance someone is to woo or charm them.

clue.text: Disorder around opening time sharing butt of ale

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for around, used with dates

indicators.note: sharing means the opening and the time overlap on one letter, so it is written once

parts.note: a hole is an opening

indicators.note: the butt of a word is its tail end, its last letter

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out at a pub's opening hour as the dregs of the beer are passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLE and ERA overlap on E, the end of ale, so it appears once: C + HOL(E)RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an infectious intestinal disease, and disorder is a medical word for illness.

clue.text: With rising hit, worth accepting group's wrongdoing

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for hit is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: worth is value or price
an act is a group of performers, such as a band

explanation.surface: Along with a chart-climbing hit, a band's value is rising, though not quite legally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is only a link word; 'rising' reverses the hit, and 'accepting' places the group inside worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Malpractice is improper or negligent professional conduct, a form of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Tried to keep right in range

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the word for range holds the letter

parts.note: a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to stay on the right side within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests extent; it is a cooking range.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: strove is the past tense of strive, to try hard.

clue.text: 'Astarte' mistakenly describing goddess

indicators.note: describing is used in its sense of drawing round, so the two words enclose the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Someone has wrongly labelled a figure as the Phoenician deity Astarte.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks tempt an anagram of Astarte, but the letters do not match; the answer spans astARTE MIStakenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon, an example of a goddess.

clue.text: Man weaker when distressed?

parts.note: read dis-tressed: the biblical strongman lost his strength when his hair (tresses) was cut off by Delilah

explanation.surface: A man is enfeebled when he is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges the strongman's power lay in his uncut hair, so being shorn left him weak.

clue.text: Got back in clothes, topless, clothing body

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the shortened word surrounds the body
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: being in clothes is being dressed
a posse is a body of people

explanation.surface: Someone recovered, getting dressed after going topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clothes' as a phrase means clothed; 'topless' drops its first letter, and 'clothing' then wraps it round the body of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to take back goods not paid for, so the past tense means got back.

clue.text: Official will copy gossip old boy's penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as an animal is shut in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to prate is to chatter idly, to gossip
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A boy from school has written down some chit-chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the legal proving of a will, and a probate copy is the court-certified official version.

clue.text: Fervent reportedly burn after transgression

indicators.note: after places the sound-alike piece behind the transgression

parts.note: a sin is a transgression against a moral law

indicators.note: reportedly means we take how the word for burn is heard rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: to sear is to burn or scorch

explanation.surface: A hellfire preacher warns that burning follows sin.
explanation.walkthrough: CERE (a waxy patch on a bird's beak) is pronounced like SEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonyms: fervent feeling is heartfelt and genuine, which is what sincere describes.

clue.text: Stop state terrorism's onset

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of terrorism's is used

explanation.surface: A call to halt state-sponsored terror at its very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop state' looks like a noun phrase about a country, but state is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to avert a disaster is to prevent or stop it happening.

clue.text: Criminal turning over brave pretended nothing's missing

indicators.note: missing tells us the letter for nothing goes absent from its place and turns up at the end
turning over signals that the joined words for brave and pretended are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to brave a danger is to dare it
posed means pretended, as in posed as a doctor
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A crook rolling over, having bluffed bravely that nothing was gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses DARE + POSED to DESOPERAD; 'missing' lifts out the O (nothing) and it reappears at the end. The blog reads 'over' as a cricket O instead, giving the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a kind of criminal from the Wild West.

clue.text: Most ingratiating hosts in small, manservant's housing

indicators.note: in puts the word for hosts inside the other letters
housing means the outside letters that enclose the word, here of manservant

parts.note: hosts are armies, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: A valet serves large crowds of guests in a cramped house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' takes M and T, the outer letters of manservant; 'in' puts ARMIES between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes an oily, unctuous manner, so the superlative means the most fawning.

clue.text: Reveal extreme skill flipping in restaurant

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the three joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to air a view is to reveal it
OTT, over the top, means extreme
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A chef shows off flashy tossing skills in a dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses AIR + OTT + ART. OTT is British shorthand for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eatery, a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Lay person consumed for love in affair

indicators.note: for means one thing replaces another, so the word for consumed swaps in

parts.note: an amour is a love affair
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone eaten up with passion during a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' suggests sex, fitting the surface, but means non-professional. ATE replaces O in AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay means non-professional, so a lay person in a field is someone without professional training.

clue.text: Doing addition, carrying about two initially

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for carrying goes round the letter

parts.note: toting means carrying

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of two is used

explanation.surface: A pupil doing a sum, carrying the two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' reads as the arithmetic term from the surface, but means toting.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add figures together, so totting means doing addition.

clue.text: Drugged states producing rushes, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word for rushes is taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: hies is an old word for hurries or rushes

explanation.surface: Narcotics produce a sudden surge of euphoria, people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rushes' looks like the drug sensation, matching the surface, but it is the verb hurries.
explanation.definitionFit: A high is the euphoric condition brought on by a drug, so plural states of intoxication.

clue.text: Nurse with occasion to hold some underwear up

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the word for occasion goes round the reversed garment

parts.note: an hour is a time or occasion, as in the hour of need

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bra is a piece of underwear

explanation.surface: A nurse picks a moment to hike up some lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' is the verb, as in nurse a grudge, not the hospital worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a grudge is to harbour it, keeping a feeling alive in the mind.

clue.text: Pregnant girl regularly hungry

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of girl

parts.note: avid means eager, hungry for something

explanation.surface: An expectant girl keeps feeling peckish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravid is a formal or medical word for carrying young, a synonym for expecting.

clue.text: Some property, say, rapidly changing hands

indicators.note: changing hands means swapping the right-hand letter for the left-hand one

parts.note: to chatter is to talk rapidly

explanation.surface: An auctioneer gabbles as goods pass quickly between buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in CHATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal property, such as furniture.

clue.text: Pliable explosive's first ignited

indicators.note: first says the word for ignited comes in front of the explosive

parts.note: lit means ignited
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: Plastic explosive is the first thing to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pliable explosive' reads as one phrase like plastic explosive, but the definition ends at Pliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: lithe means supple and flexible, bending easily.

clue.text: Mostly fresh sailors in vessels

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: more means additional or fresh, as in fresh supplies
tars are sailors

explanation.surface: A crew of new seamen are aboard ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' points to ships, but here it means bowls: a mortar is the bowl a pestle grinds in.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortars are sturdy bowls for pounding ingredients, a kind of container or vessel.

clue.text: Battle of terrorists is erratically repelled

indicators.note: repelled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fight in which terrorists are driven back in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratically' looks like an anagram signal but only carries letters; reading backwards in terroriSTS IS ERratically gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To battle against something is to fight it, to resist it.

clue.text: Sensitive sweetheart — drive to welcome sex returned

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to drive something is to move it along

indicators.note: returned means the word for sex is read backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A tender lover with an urge to embrace intimacy again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' gives the centre of sweet, not a lover. 'returned' reverses the word for sex, and 'to welcome' puts it inside drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive issue stirs strong feelings, which is what emotive means.

clue.text: Scattered silver pieces sailor found among fish

indicators.note: found among places the first pieces within the young fish

parts.note: fry are young fish
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
men are the pieces in chess or draughts
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman finds pieces of silver in a fish's belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragmentary evidence is broken up and disconnected, spread in scattered bits.
